newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Zhuzhou smelter not short LME zinc - source.
newsitem.headline: China's Zhuzhou smelter not short LME zinc - source.

text.p: An official at a major Chinese zinc producer said on Friday the smelter was not short on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and denied it had been forced to crank up production of the metal because it was over-committed.
"It is not possible that we sold forward our whole year's production, the official at the Zhuzhou smelter, who did not wish to be identified, said by telephone.
"It is not possible that we are producing at more than our annual capacity of 250,000 tonnes," he said.
"These are just rumours," the official said.
A percentage of the smelter's zinc was sold on long-term contracts, the official said, but refused to elaborate on quantity or terms.
He also refused to say how much of the smelter's zinc had been sold on the LME or how much was currently stored in LME warehouses.

Speaking by telephone from the smelter, the official also denied rumours that have circulated in the market for months that Zhuzhou sold options at between $1,200 and $1,350 a tonne and now that prices have soared to close to $1,500, it was suffering substantial losses.
LME zinc prices have scored gains of $150 a tonne in the past week, and raced up to a peak of $1,495 a tonne on Thursday before profit-taking took some of the shine off the advance.
The last trade was at $1,476 a tonne. Traders throughout Asia said they expected prices to breach $1,500 when the market opened on Friday.

He said Swiss trading house Glencore had recently complained about the quality of 100 tonnes of Zhuzhou zinc, making a possible quality claim to the LME against Zhuzhou's registered Torch brand speical high grade zinc.
This problem had been resolved, he said.
In a statement received by Reuters in Singapore on Monday, Zhuzhou said the claim had been withdrawn last week because no quality problems could be found.
Another Zhuzhou source confirmed the trading firm involved was Glencore. Glencore executives in Asia could not be reached for comment on Friday.

Customers had begun complaining in early 1997 about the quality of Zhuzhou's Torch brand zinc, during shipments to Japan to comply with its General System of Preferences (GSP) imports from developing countries, a source close to Glencore said.
"Usually our customers prefer Torch over HX (made by the Huludao smelter) but in the first quarter of this year they started to say they wanted HX," he said.
Recent market talk has referred to a Chinese producer, widely believed to be Zhuzhou, as being short by anything between 60,000 tonnes and 400,000 tonnes.

LME broker Macquarie referred in its Wednesday market report to widespread talk in the zinc market of a squeeze being engineered by one major trade house, possibly in association with some producers, adding that the "victims" were said to be Chinese producers short between 200,000 and 400,000 tonnes.
A couple of traders said on Friday Zhuzhou had committed its total 1997 production, and that the smelter was producing at 110-120 percent of capacity to make up for its short position.
Zhouzhou released figures in May showing production for the first four months of 1997 at 93,821 tonnes, up 185 percent from the same period in 1996.
Zhuzhou had moved substantial tonnages of its zinc metal to LME warehouses in Singapore to take advantage of good LME prices, other sources at the smelter have said.
The smelter said earlier this year it was re-refining old ingots to boost output, and traders have said this, coupled with boosted output, could lead to possible quality problems.
-- Lynne O'Donnell, Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
